fields.narrative_intro: *A frazzled person and a scatterbrained person discuss Ataraxos's Stratego victory inside a dying startup's final all-hands meeting.*
fields.panel1:
[setup]
FRAZZLED PERSON: "Ataraxos beat Pim Niemeijer 15–1, with four draws."
SCATTERBRAINED PERSON: "Our final all-hands has already produced four draws."
fields.panel2:
[build]
FRAZZLED PERSON: "DeepMind's 2022 DeepNash couldn't crack Stratego."
SCATTERBRAINED PERSON: "Ataraxos did it with 16 GPUs and a few thousand dollars."
fields.panel3:
[pivot]
FRAZZLED PERSON: "Forty pieces hide across more than a decillion setups."
SCATTERBRAINED PERSON: "Our startup hides one runway number across forty spreadsheets."
fields.panel4:
[silent reaction]
[Visual: A giant Stratego board covers the meeting table; forty face-down tiles sit beside forty spreadsheets. A tiny Ataraxos scans them while both people freeze.]
fields.panel5:
[punch]
FRAZZLED PERSON: "It can reason through 2,000 moves of uncertainty and bluffing."
SCATTERBRAINED PERSON: "Then it found our runway: one move."
fields.panel6:
[button]
[Visual: The final tile flips to “RUNWAY: ONE MOVE”; the whole office folds into a Stratego box labeled “FINAL ALL-HANDS.”]

narrative_summary: At a doomed startup's final all-hands, Ataraxos applies Stratego-level uncertainty management and discovers the company's runway is only one move.
rationale: Candidate 1 uses the story’s specific facts while turning hidden information into a sharper startup visual: a runway reduced to “one move.” Candidate 2 is clean and well-structured, but its uncertainty/payroll joke is a more familiar startup-collapse framing and lands less decisively.
story_title: With most information hidden, the game Stratego had stumped AI until now
place: inside a dying startup's final all-hands meeting
hat_pair: oversized foam question mark worn as a hat
foam emergency brake handle worn as a hat with a red warning tag dangling from the brim
